content.title: About
content.content: Palm hearts are the tender, heart‑shaped cores of young palm shoots. After harvesting they are usually boiled or canned. They have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a crisp‑yet‑tender texture. Commonly used in salads, appetizers, warm dishes, and vegetarian recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Palm hearts are often called “tropical artichokes,” although they are unrelated to true artichokes.
They are traditionally harvested in Southeast Asia, especially Thailand, Indonesia and the Philippines.
Collecting the hearts requires removing outer leaves and part of the stem, making the product a delicacy.
Canned palm hearts keep for a long time without loss of flavor or nutrients.
In some cultures they are featured in ceremonial dishes and festive feasts.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Cooked palm hearts contain about 20 kcal per 100 g, making them an excellent choice for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium aids normal heart and muscle function and helps maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B1, B2 and B6 participate in energy metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Phenolic compounds in palm hearts help combat free radicals.

items.title: Palm allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to palm hearts.

items.title: Sodium content in canned versions
items.content: Canned palm hearts often contain added salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium options.

items.title: Limited fresh availability
items.content: Fresh palm hearts are harvested in specific regions and may not be readily available in regular stores.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Palm hearts can be eaten cold in salads, added to vegetable stews, used as fillings for pies or vegetarian burgers. Before use they are usually rinsed and sliced. They can also be lightly sautéed with olive oil and herbs for a warm side dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked or canned palm hearts in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. Canned versions can be kept in a cool, dry place until the expiration date on the label. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.
